processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Strain rate range 0.1–10 s^-1. Hot deformation triggers dynamic recrystallization: DDRX at high temperature/high strain rate, CDRX at lower temperature/low strain rate.

structures.overall_structure: Ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy undergoing dynamic recrystallization during hot torsion: discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX) at high temperature/high strain rate and continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) at lower temperature/low strain rate.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Temperature range 900–1100 °C; strain rate range 0.1–10 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: Study effects of strain, strain rate, and temperature on dynamic recrystallization of the ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy
characterization_methods.key_findings: DDRX at high temperature/high strain rate; CDRX at lower temperature/low strain rate

characterization_methods.technique: strain rate–temperature processing map (DDRX activation domain)
characterization_methods.purpose: Map the activation domain of DDRX in the Fe-8% Al ferritic steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: DDRX activated at high strain rate; not activated at low strain rate; critical strain rate boundary decreases as temperature rises (from between 1 and 10 s^-1 at 850 °C to just above 0.1 s^-1 at ~1150 °C); data columns at 900, 1000, 1100 °C.

unmapped_findings: Ferritic Fe-Al alloys often exhibit surface defects referred to as roping after deep drawing, mainly attributed to the inhomogeneous orientation distribution of individual grains; promoting a recrystallized structure by DDRX seems advantageous to limit roping (b0036, b0038).
Depending on the deformation conditions, there is a competition between DDRX and CDRX in the Fe-8 wt.% Al ferritic alloy (b0038).

The DDRX activation domain in the Fe-8% Al ferritic steel is delimited by a critical strain rate that decreases as temperature rises; experimental points lie in three vertical columns at 900, 1000 and 1100 °C (figure_006).
